notes:
Account background: Emberlane is a mid-market SaaS that builds conversational assistants for B2B product teams. Previously on IncumbentAI (API); started seeing regressions in streaming/tok-by-tok latency in Q4-2025 — reports from product/UX teams 'streaming lag kills the conversational flow'.

Sales/eng summary: evaluating Redwood Hosted API first for fast rollout and streaming reliability. Plan to pilot with 50 internal agents (beta) then scale to 500+ concurrent sessions. Strong interest in Dedicated once SLA/throughput math is validated. Very cost-conscious but willing to commit for predictable latency.

Security: needs SSO/SAML integration, audit logs, and KMS. Data residency ask for EU for one large customer vertical. Legal wants retention controls.

POC ask from Emberlane: 48h sustained chat workload with tool-calls (calendar lookup, internal KB fetch), streaming latency SLA of median <=400ms/token under typical concurrent load, graceful fallbacks if model variant unavailable.

Stated pain: "We can tolerate occasional cost variability, but UX regressions are non-negotiable" — CTO (Mar 2 call).

Current positioning: Redwood considered primary replacement if POC numbers hold. Sales path: hosted -> dedicated (6-12 month commit).

poc_results: Redwood hosted streaming median per-token latency: 280-420ms (varies by sequence prefix; median ~330ms) under 50 concurrent sessions.
Incumbent API cohort observed median per-token latency: 650-1200ms with frequent spikes during bursts (>1500ms).
Throughput: Redwood handled 100 concurrent agent sessions with acceptable latency degradation (p95 ~720ms) when prefix caching enabled; incumbent p95 >1500ms under same load.
Tool calling stability: Redwood handled 98/100 calendar lookups (retries auto-handled); incumbent 83/100 with timeouts seen during heavy bursts.
Observed benefits: streaming incremental tokens arrived faster enabling earlier UI updates; prefix/KV cache reduced repeated prompt cost ~18% on benchmark workload.
Known issues: one tool-call pattern triggers 504 on our harness; SE investigating routing/fallback behavior for that pattern (ticket RED-1310).
